ops.title: Decide whether ccx vcs ship's path operands are literal pathspecs or globs
ops.description:
Two hand-built pathspecs reach git WITHOUT `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`:
`internal/cli/shipselect_git.go:112` (`add -A -- <whole...>` via `render.RunCLIEnv`)
and `:51` (`restore --staged -- <paths...>` via `render.RunCLI`).

So a shipped path like `docs/[id].md`, or one starting with `:`, globs or is read
as pathspec magic instead of addressing itself.

They could not be centralized when found (2026-08-03): `internal/vcs`'s
`gitRun` appends `-z` unconditionally (`gitrun.go:74`), which these MUTATING
verbs reject, and `gitLiteralPathspecs` (`gitrun.go:17`) is unexported. The fix
shape is a mutating sibling to `gitRun` — same `GitArgs` slots, no `-z`.

**This is deliberately not a fold-in.** It is a user-visible semantic decision:
today `ccx vcs ship 'src/*.go'` globs, and making pathspecs literal would change
what that means for users. Same question applies to `ship.go:507` and
`shipgt.go:328`.

Blast radius today is a user shipping an exotically named path, so this is a
decision to make deliberately rather than an outage to fix. Surfaced by the
hunks/shipselect centralization lane, which fixed the READ-side instance
(`hunks.go` `changedFiles` → `vcs.GitPaths`) and correctly declined this one.

ops.text: A decision is recorded on whether 'ccx vcs ship src/*.go' should glob (today's behavior) or address a literal file named src/*.go
shipselect_git.go:51 and :112 either move onto a centralized mutating git runner carrying GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, or carry a comment recording the deliberate choice not to
